articles.title: Build parametric 3D CAD parts from Claude Code with SolidCraft MCP
articles.excerpt: If you have tried to get an AI agent to make a real, editable 3D part, you have probably hit the same wall: it writes an STL or a pile of OpenSCAD, and the moment you want to change one dimension you…
articles.body: If you have tried to get an AI agent to make a real, editable 3D part, you have probably hit the same wall: it writes an STL or a pile of OpenSCAD, and the moment you want to change one dimension you start over. A parametric CAD tool with a feature timeline fixes that, and SolidCraft is one that ships with its own MCP server. tangency-labs/solidcraft is an open-source parametric 3D CAD application written in pure Rust. Per the README you sketch, constrain and build solids on a parametric feature timeline, change a dimension and watch the model rebuild, and run it on desktop, in the browser, or let AI agents model through the built-in MCP server. This post walks through the setup for Claude Code and what to expect.
articles.author: Deduped

articles.title: How I pick which search queries to push on a new site
articles.excerpt: I run a small information site alone, with an AI coding tool doing most of the page generation. Making pages turned out to be the easy part. Deciding which search queries to push first was the part I…
articles.body: I run a small information site alone, with an AI coding tool doing most of the page generation. Making pages turned out to be the easy part. Deciding which search queries to push first was the part I had no rule for, so I wrote a deliberately simple one. The data I export 28 days from Search Console and look at queries and pages. For this site that was 44 clicks, 2,820 impressions, a 1.6% CTR and an average position of 8.2, across 126 queries and 439 pages. The rule I look for queries where: the average position is roughly 6-12, there are impressions, there are almost no clicks. That band is the bottom of page one or the start of page two. A title and first paragraph change is cheap, and it is the zone where a small change can plausibly move the result.

articles.title: Building a Personal English Curriculum Like You'd Scope a Software Project
articles.excerpt: Developers are good at one thing many language learners never do: scoping. Before we write code, we ask what the feature is for, who uses it, and what "done" looks like. Yet when most of us decide to…
articles.body: Developers are good at one thing many language learners never do: scoping. Before we write code, we ask what the feature is for, who uses it, and what "done" looks like. Yet when most of us decide to improve our English, we open a textbook at chapter one and hope the scope sorts itself out. It rarely does. If you work in tech and English is not your first language, you already know where the friction shows up. It is not in reading documentation; most of us can do that. It is in the daily standup when you need to explain a blocker in two sentences, in a code review comment that has to sound direct without sounding rude, or in a technical interview where you have to think aloud under pressure.

articles.title: Hyperliquid Trading Bot: What to Backtest First
articles.excerpt: Before you trust a Hyperliquid trading bot, backtest its net result after fees, slippage and funding, then check whether that result survives on data the bot has never seen. If it does, run it in pape…
articles.body: Before you trust a Hyperliquid trading bot, backtest its net result after fees, slippage and funding, then check whether that result survives on data the bot has never seen. If it does, run it in paper trading on live prices, because a backtest alone can't show how the bot handles real market conditions. New bots and bold screenshots tend to appear wherever attention goes, so it helps to know how to test them. This guide makes no claim about where prices go next. First, define what you are testing "Hyperliquid trading bot" can mean two different things: A bot that trades the HYPE token , on any venue that lists it. A bot that executes on the Hyperliquid exchange , on any of its markets. The two have different risks. The first depends on one asset's price history.

articles.title: Python or JavaScript First? Decide by the Job You Want — A 2-Question Test
articles.excerpt: Python or JavaScript First? Decide by the Job You Want — A 2-Question Test "Python or JavaScript?" is the question almost every beginner asks first, and the internet answers it with salary tables and…
articles.body: Python or JavaScript First? Decide by the Job You Want — A 2-Question Test "Python or JavaScript?" is the question almost every beginner asks first, and the internet answers it with salary tables and arguments about syntax. Both are the wrong way to decide. Your first language is not a lifetime commitment. It is the tool you will use to get your first real projects finished and, for many people, a first job. So decide by the work, not by the debate. Two questions settle it in about ten minutes. Answer them honestly, on paper, and the choice usually makes itself. Question 1: What do you want to have built six months from now? Picture one finished thing — not a course certificate, an actual project you can show someone.

articles.title: How I Extended a Refaster Rule in Picnic's error-prone-support (and Recovered a PR GitHub Broke)
articles.excerpt: This is post 4 in my open source series. After Zalando Logbook and the Adyen Java library, this one is about Picnic's error-prone-support, and it has a twist: the PR I opened got stuck in a broken sta…
articles.body: This is post 4 in my open source series. After Zalando Logbook and the Adyen Java library, this one is about Picnic's error-prone-support , and it has a twist: the PR I opened got stuck in a broken state on GitHub, and I had to recreate it. What is error-prone-support? error-prone-support is an open source project from Picnic. It extends Google's Error Prone with extra bug checks and Refaster rules . A Refaster rule says "this code pattern should be rewritten like this", and it can fix it automatically across a codebase. What I worked on The project already had a rule called RequireNonNullExpression . I extended it to cover this pattern: // Before: Optional.of() throws a NullPointerException if value is null, // so the Optional can never be empty. The orElse() part is dead code.

articles.body: Ahead of the release of Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI , Nintendo is launching its own fall juggernaut: a Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . The remake, which is releasing 28 years after the launch of the original version on Nintendo 64, has a much more realistic visual style and some modern improvements like a jump button, a way to sprint, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” feature that helps you keep track of your progress. But while the game has a new coat of paint, it appears many elements will still remain faithful to the classic N64 release. Nintendo has also launched a special version of the Switch 2 and Switch 2 Pro Controller with Triforce imagery to celebrate the game.

articles.body: NASA is reviving discussions to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope, which is operating well but is on track to reenter Earth's atmosphere about six years from now. The agency issued a request for information (RFI) on Oct. 29 for "in-space servicing" capabilities, which could include boosting Hubble's orbit (which is naturally degrading due to atmospheric drag), or even a mission to "enhance its capabilities" in some way. articles.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
articles.excerpt: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Tele…
articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

articles.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
articles.excerpt: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart.
articles.body: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement .
